answers.question: What does “¿me pone…?” do in a Spanish bar?
answers.answer: orders something: could you give me / I’ll have
answers.writer_claim: orders food or drink, like Can I get…?

answers.question: After para, “mí” or “me”, and is there an accent?
Is “sitio” the usual word for room/space at a restaurant in Spain?
Which form is “recomienda”: tú or usted?
Which form is “perdone” and can “¡oiga!” sound abrupt?
answers.answer: usted imperative; yes, oiga can sound abrupt

answers.question: Natural: “sin cebolla” or “sin la cebolla” when ordering?
Back-translate “la paella está muy rica”; what does “es rico” mean about a person?
answers.answer: the paella is really tasty; he is rich
answers.writer_claim: the paella is really good; has money

answers.question: Standard answer in Spain when done ordering?
Back-translate “¿Se puede pagar con tarjeta?”
answers.answer: Can you / can I pay by card?

answers.question: If a friend says “te invito” in Spain, who pays?
